why: write() opens the output file on the first row and nothing on the write path closes it. close() closes self._fh and marks the exporter closed; write() raises on a closed exporter, so a later write cannot reopen the file in 'w' mode and truncate it. __exit__ (further down the file) calls close(), and the only user, app/jobs.py, holds the Exporter in a with block, so the file is closed on success and on error. Not creating a file for an empty export is the stated purpose (the docstring in the hunk).
